architecture.mechanism: Estimate propagation vectors from paired forward/backward (unilateral) and bilateral measurements, then combine those vector estimates using an adaptive threshold to reconstruct missing data at occluded "holes," producing a high-fidelity interpolated field while suppressing block artifacts.
architecture.intervention: Fit the Silverado 1500 LD underbody with a structural-health monitoring grid—ultrasonic thickness, EIS and optical sensors mounted on opposing (forward/backward) faces of the frame rails and driveline housings—estimate corrosion-propagation vectors per frame block, combine them with an adaptive threshold scaled to local alloy, coating and road-exposure severity, and interpolate thickness across unmeasured/occluded regions (behind driveline components, inside boxed rails) to generate a complete corrosion map that triggers targeted recoating or panel replacement.
architecture.expected_effect: Early, spatially complete detection of rust and corrosion—including hidden regions that visual inspection misses—with fewer false-positive artifact calls, so corroded metal is treated before section loss compromises frame stiffness, crash energy absorption or driveline alignment, preserving structural integrity and durability.
architecture.falsification_test: On an instrumented truck, deliberately mask selected frame and driveline regions to create measurement "holes," run the bilateral-plus-adaptive-threshold interpolation, then strip and teardown-measure true wall thickness at those masked sites; the mechanism is falsified if interpolated thickness error at occluded sites is not significantly lower (paired t-test, p<0.05) than naive nearest-neighbor extrapolation, or if artifact (false corrosion) rates exceed those of fixed-threshold thresholding.
